content.title: About
content.content: Split pea soup with meat is a classic Russian dish made from dried peas, meat (usually beef or pork), vegetables, and spices. The soup is thick, hearty, and carries the distinctive earthy flavor of peas combined with the richness of meat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pea soup has been a staple in Russian cuisine since medieval times.
Traditional recipes often include smoked ham or bacon, giving the broth a subtle smoky aroma.
In some regions the soup is finished with sautéed carrots or a spoonful of sauerkraut for extra tang.
Even after long cooking, peas retain a high proportion of their nutrients.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peas provide about 25 % protein, making the soup a good protein source, especially if the meat is reduced or replaced with plant alternatives.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: Meat contributes easily absorbed iron and zinc, essential for immune function and energy production.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Peas have a low GI, which helps maintain stable glucose levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The soup supplies B1, B6, and folate, supporting nervous system health and metabolism.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Using ready‑made broth or adding excessive salt can make the soup too salty.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Peas can cause gas in sensitive stomachs; soaking them before cooking reduces this effect.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Serve the soup hot, often with a slice of rye bread or croutons. Garnish with fresh parsley or dill and a dollop of sour cream if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge and reheat gently on the stove.
